subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which equation correctly states Hooke's law?
questions.explain: Hooke's law is F = k × x, where the force is directly proportional to the extension.

questions.q: What defines elastic deformation?
options: The object returns to its original shape when the force is removed
The object keeps its new shape after the force is removed
The object melts when the force is applied
The object always breaks when stretched
questions.explain: In elastic deformation the object recovers its original shape and size once the deforming force is removed.

questions.q: What is inelastic deformation?
options: Deformation where the object does not return to its original shape when the force is removed
Deformation that only happens to springs
questions.explain: After inelastic deformation the object remains permanently distorted even after the force is removed.

questions.q: What is the unit of the spring constant?
questions.explain: Spring constant k = force ÷ extension, so its unit is newtons per metre (N/m).

questions.q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure is measured in pascals, where one pascal equals one newton per square metre.

questions.q: Which equation gives the energy stored in a stretched spring (within the limit of proportionality)?
questions.explain: Elastic potential energy stored is E = ½ k x².

questions.q: Which equation gives the pressure difference due to a column of liquid?
options: pressure = height × density × gravitational field strength
questions.explain: The pressure due to a fluid column is p = h × ρ × g.

questions.q: What name is given to the upward force a fluid exerts on a submerged object?
questions.explain: The resultant upward force from fluid pressure acting on a submerged object is called upthrust.

questions.q: What does the limit of proportionality of a spring represent?
options: The point beyond which extension is no longer directly proportional to force
The point at which the spring snaps
The force needed to compress the spring fully
The maximum energy a spring can store
questions.explain: Up to the limit of proportionality, force and extension are directly proportional; beyond it the relationship becomes non-linear.

questions.q: On a force–extension graph for a spring obeying Hooke's law, what shape is the line?
options: A straight line through the origin
questions.explain: While force is proportional to extension the graph is a straight line passing through the origin.

questions.q: An object floats in a liquid. What is true about the forces on it?
options: The upthrust equals the weight of the object
The weight is greater than the upthrust
There is no gravitational force acting
questions.explain: A floating object is in equilibrium, so the upthrust balances its weight.

questions.q: Why does the pressure in a liquid increase with depth?
options: There is a greater weight of liquid above pressing down
The liquid becomes less dense deeper down
Gravity is stronger deeper in the liquid
questions.explain: Deeper points support a taller column of liquid, so the weight of liquid above and hence the pressure is greater.

questions.q: What does the area under a force–extension graph represent?
options: The work done in stretching the spring
questions.explain: The area under a force–extension graph equals the work done, which is stored as elastic potential energy.

questions.q: A spring is stretched well beyond its limit of proportionality and the force is then removed. What is the likely result?
options: It remains permanently longer than its original length
It returns exactly to its original length
questions.explain: Stretching past the elastic limit causes inelastic deformation, so the spring stays permanently distorted.

questions.q: How does atmospheric pressure change as altitude increases?
options: It first increases then falls to zero at ground level
questions.explain: At higher altitude there is less air above pushing down, so atmospheric pressure falls.

questions.q: A spring obeys Hooke's law. If the force applied is doubled, what happens to the extension?
questions.explain: Because extension is directly proportional to force, doubling the force doubles the extension.

questions.q: A force of 12 N stretches a spring by 0.06 m. What is the spring constant?
A spring has a spring constant of 25 N/m. What extension is produced by a force of 5 N?
A point is 2 m below the surface of water of density 1000 kg/m³ (g = 10 N/kg). What is the pressure due to the water?
